---
description: "How NCodeGroup .NET code allocates, sizes, pools, zeroes and disposes byte, char and secret buffers, and the span and buffer-writer shapes its APIs use to stay off the heap."
applyTo: "**/*.cs"
---

# Allocations and buffers

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Cap the size of every response from an untrusted outbound fetch twice: reject on the advertised Content-Length, and enforce a hard byte limit while streaming the body.** A Content-Length that is missing or false must not be able to exhaust memory. *Check:* Flag untrusted responses read with ReadAsStringAsync, ReadAsByteArrayAsync or an unbounded stream copy. Also flag code that trusts Content-Length alone and does not count bytes as it reads. <sub>Identity ADR-0095</sub>
- **Keep secret material (passwords, keys, tokens, decrypted plaintext, and their decoded or re-encoded intermediate copies) in sensitive buffers from NCode.Buffers, such as `BufferFactory.CreatePooledBufferWriter(isSensitive: true)` or `BufferFactory.Rent(..., isSensitive: true, ...)`, which are pinned and zeroed on release. Never hold secrets in a `string`, and dispose the buffers as soon as they are used. Only an encrypted envelope may be a `string`.** A string, a plain array or an ordinary pooled buffer cannot be wiped reliably, so secret bytes stay in managed memory. *Check:* Flag secrets returned or held as `string`/`byte[]`, passed through `Encoding.GetString` or array-returning `Encoding.GetBytes`, or rented from `ArrayPool`, `MemoryPool.Shared` or a non-sensitive writer. Also flag sensitive rentals that are not disposed right after use. <sub>Identity ADR-0230; Identity ADR-0235; Identity ADR-0238; Identity ADR-0265; Identity review of #420; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Hold a secret that is stored in a field or kept across an `await` as a sensitive `BufferFactory.Rent(..., isSensitive: true, out Memory<byte>)` lease, never as a bare array or a `CreatePinnedArray` ref struct.** `CreatePinnedArray` returns a ref struct that only works synchronously inside one method. The lease keeps the secret pinned and zeroes it when it is returned. *Check:* Flag secrets kept in fields or used across awaits as plain arrays, and `CreatePinnedArray` results that would need to escape the method. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Encode public, non-secret material such as SPKI public keys with a non-sensitive pooled writer (`BufferFactory.CreatePooledBufferWriter(isSensitive: false)`), and keep the sensitive secure pool for secret material.** Public data does not need the more expensive pinned secure pool, while private data must never go through the non-sensitive pool. *Check:* Flag public-key or other non-secret encoding that uses a sensitive buffer, and private-key material written to a non-sensitive writer. <sub>Identity ADR-0115</sub>
- **When an operation produces output whose length is known only after it runs (decrypt, unwrap, a remote response), write it to a caller-supplied `IBufferWriter<byte>`, call `Advance` only after the operation succeeds, and zero anything already written if it fails. Use a `Span<byte>` destination with `out int bytesWritten` only when the size is known in advance.** Callers who cannot size a buffer end up guessing, which hides real errors as 'destination too small'. Secret bytes from a partly finished failed operation must not stay in the caller's buffer. *Check:* Flag unwrap/decrypt APIs that return a new `byte[]` or take a fixed Span/Memory destination for output of unknown length. Flag `Advance` called before success, failure paths that leave partial output uncleared, and callers that over-rent (for example 2x) to guess a size. <sub>Identity ADR-0279; Identity review of #370</sub>
- **When decoding (for example base64url) into a buffer, size the buffer from an upper bound or the decoder's own byte-count API, then use or verify the `bytesWritten` the decoder returns. Never trust a length you computed yourself.** A hand-computed length can be wrong for some input lengths (for example lengths that are not multiples of three), which gives a mis-sized buffer or trailing garbage. *Check:* Flag decode calls whose output length is computed ahead of time and used without checking the returned `bytesWritten` or decoded length. *Note:* The production instructions size JWS/JWE segment buffers with `Base64Url.GetByteCountForDecode` and treat slicing by bytesWritten as unnecessary. Even with an exact count API, still check that bytesWritten matches. <sub>Identity ADR-0092; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make an owned copy of any buffer or collection a caller hands you before you store it: copy `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`/`byte[]` on write to in-memory stores or caches, and buffer stored collections (injected `IEnumerable<T>` included) into FrozenSet/FrozenDictionary for lookups, ImmutableArray for iterated sequences, or List<T> only for genuinely mutable working sets.** A caller that reuses or mutates its buffer or collection would otherwise change stored state, and a lazy sequence re-enumerates on every read. *Check:* Flag stores, caches or constructors that assign a passed-in memory, array or collection straight to a member without copying it. <sub>Identity ADR-0267; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Dispose every local `IDisposable`/`IAsyncDisposable` you own with a `using var` or `await using var` declaration, unless ownership is deliberately transferred. This includes `HttpResponseMessage`, `Stream`, pooled writers, rented leases and `X509Certificate2` instances.** Undisposed resources leak native handles and pooled or secret memory. The declaration form is the house style. *Check:* Flag disposable locals without `using`, `using (...) { }` blocks, and try/finally Dispose patterns. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0116</sub>
- **Treat `X509Certificate2`/`X509Certificate2Collection` results as owned by the caller. A component that caches certificates (issuer certificates included) disposes them in its own Dispose. Resolve a request's client certificate once per request and cache it in the request items. Dispose the certificates you decoded when the request ends (for example with `HttpResponse.RegisterForDispose`), but never dispose `HttpContext.Connection.ClientCertificate`.** Certificates hold native resources. Every consumer in a request must see the same certificate, and the connection's own certificate belongs to the connection, not the request. *Check:* Flag cached certificates not disposed in Dispose, exported certificates the caller never disposes, the certificate header decoded more than once per request, and disposal of the connection's certificate. <sub>Identity ADR-0300; Identity ADR-0172</sub>
- **Use `stackalloc` only for small sizes with a constant upper bound (for example 256 bytes or less, or a fixed hash size). For caller-controlled or unbounded lengths, rent from a pool, for example stackalloc with a rented fallback.** A stackalloc sized by input can overflow the stack. *Check:* Flag `stackalloc` sized by a parameter, an input length or any value without a small constant cap. <sub>Identity ADR-0116; Identity review of #341</sub>
- **Rent transient buffers and accumulating writers from NCode.Buffers `BufferFactory` (`CreatePooledBufferWriter`, `Rent`, `CreatePinnedArray`) or use a small fixed `stackalloc`, instead of `new byte[]`, `.ToArray()`, `new ArrayBufferWriter<byte>`, `MemoryStream`, `GC.AllocateArray` or `JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes`. Allocate an array only when an external API requires one (and then get it from a rented buffer with `MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray`), or when the data must outlive the call and belong to a longer-lived object.** Transient arrays add GC pressure on hot paths and can leave secrets on the heap. One pooled convention keeps zeroing wired in. *Check:* Flag short-lived `new byte[...]`, `.ToArray()`, `new ArrayBufferWriter<byte>()`, `new MemoryStream()`, `SerializeToUtf8Bytes` or bare `ArrayPool<byte>.Shared` in new code where nothing requires an array. *Note:* The review of #316 accepted `ArrayPool<byte>` as an alternative. ADR-0116 and the production instructions, which are more specific, require BufferFactory instead. <sub>Identity ADR-0116; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity review of #316; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **When a pooled writer that is a `using` local must be passed to a `ref TWriter` API, keep the `using var` for disposal and pass a separate non-using `IBufferWriter<byte>` local that refers to the same writer.** A using local cannot be passed by ref (CS1657), and removing `using` to get around that leaks the pooled buffer. *Check:* Flag pooled writers whose `using` was removed so they could be passed by ref. <sub>Identity ADR-0116</sub>
- **Give APIs that produce binary data (encode, export, serialize, key/DER material, JSON records, stream-body reads) `ReadOnlySpan<T>`/`ReadOnlyMemory<T>` inputs, and have them write to a caller-supplied generic `ref TWriter destination` where `TWriter : IBufferWriter<byte>, allows ref struct`, or to a `Utf8JsonWriter`, instead of returning a new `byte[]` or `string`.** This avoids per-call allocations, lets callers choose pooled or sensitive storage, accepts ref struct writers without boxing, and lets readers parse straight from a pooled `ReadOnlySequence<byte>` with no copy. *Check:* Flag new or changed methods that return `byte[]` or take `byte[]` parameters for binary data. Flag a plain `IBufferWriter<byte>` parameter where the generic `allows ref struct` form would work; when the plain form is needed (for example to feed a Utf8JsonWriter), the reason should be documented. Flag body-read helpers that return arrays, and callers that call `ToArray()` before a parse that accepts a sequence. When a ref struct writer is the destination of `Utf8JsonWriter` output, stage the output in a pooled buffer and copy it. <sub>Identity ADR-0111; Identity ADR-0115; Identity ADR-0116; Identity ADR-0283; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity review of #382; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Give each public producer that writes to a caller-supplied span or writer a public sizing method on the same type (`GetXxxLength`/`GetByteCount`). When a public encode or decode method takes a `Span<byte>` destination, also give it an `IBufferWriter<byte>` (`ref TWriter`) overload.** Callers can then size destinations exactly, or skip sizing and allocating altogether. *Check:* Flag new span- or writer-based Write/Wrap/Encode/Decode methods that have no matching length method, and span-only public encode/decode methods that have no buffer-writer overload. <sub>Identity ADR-0279; Identity ADR-0235; Identity review of #375; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Get a contiguous span from a multi-segment `Sequence<byte>`/`ReadOnlySequence<byte>` with the shared `GetSpanLease(isSensitive:)` helper, never with `.ToArray()` or by concatenating segments by hand.** The helper leases a contiguous view without allocating, and zeroes it when the data is sensitive. *Check:* Flag `.ToArray()` on sequences and hand-written loops that copy segments to flatten a sequence. <sub>Identity ADR-0116; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Use the `out Span<T>` overload of `BufferFactory.Rent` by default, use `out Memory<T>` only for buffers kept in a field or used across an `await`, and never slice the returned buffer back to the requested length.** The out buffer is already exactly the requested length, and Span is cheaper for local, synchronous use. *Check:* Flag `.Slice(0, length)` or range slices on a buffer returned by `Rent`, and `out Memory<T>` used only locally and synchronously. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When a serializer has to hand back transient bytes, return a disposable rented-buffer lease that the caller disposes with `using`, not a new `byte[]`, and document that consumers must copy the value before their write completes.** This removes the allocation, and the buffer can go back to the pool safely once the consumer has copied it. *Check:* Flag serialize methods that return a `byte[]` which is written to a store and then dropped. <sub>Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Hash without heap allocations. Use the span overloads (`SHA256.HashData(source, destination)`) into a `stackalloc` destination of the hash size. Feed multi-part input through `IncrementalHash.AppendData` instead of concatenating it. Compute thumbprints from raw DER bytes rather than building an `X509Certificate2` per candidate. When the same fixed-size hash runs several times in a row, allocate the output buffer once in the caller and pass it in as a `Span<byte>`.** Hash outputs are small and fixed in size. Concatenating input, creating certificate objects and allocating per call all add allocations and native resources that a hash or thumbprint check does not need. *Check:* Flag array-returning `HashData`/`ComputeHash` whose result is only encoded or compared, prefix+message concatenation done only to hash it, `X509Certificate2` created in loops just for a thumbprint, and repeated hashing helpers that each allocate their own output. <sub>Identity ADR-0107; Identity ADR-0116; Identity ADR-0273; Identity review of #341; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Back immutable JSON-wrapping models, and records you read back, with a detached `JsonElement` from `JsonElement.Parse`/`JsonElement.ParseValue`, rather than a mutable `JsonObject` that needs defensive `DeepClone` calls or a `JsonDocument` kept alive.** A detached JsonElement is immutable and owns no pooled `JsonDocument`, so there is nothing to clone or dispose. *Check:* Flag immutable models that store a `JsonObject` and DeepClone it, `JsonDocument` instances held just to keep an element, and `JsonDocument.Parse` used to read back stored records. <sub>Identity ADR-0119; Identity ADR-0283</sub>
- **Produce a `string` only once, at a storage or wire boundary, with `string.Create`. Pass span inputs through a readonly ref struct state and check the written count against the length. Do not fill a rented char buffer and then call `new string(span)`.** `string.Create` writes in place with no extra copy, and the count check stops a '\0' remainder from being persisted. *Check:* Flag `new string(span)` after filling a rented buffer, and `string.Create` callbacks that do not check the written count. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Read and parse text as `ReadOnlySpan<char>`. Give helpers that only read text a span parameter, and keep `string` on public contract types. Slice instead of calling `Substring`, split with `MemoryExtensions.Split` into a stack `Range` buffer instead of `string.Split`, and compare with span `StartsWith`/`Equals`. For compact JWS/JWE tokens, allocate `segmentCount + 1` ranges, reject any other segment count, and take the signing input as a slice of the original text.** Span parameters accept existing string callers and slices with no allocation. Range splitting allocates no substrings, and the spare range slot catches extra segments. *Check:* Flag `string.Split`, `Substring`, read-only helpers that take a `string`, Range buffers with no spare slot, and JWS signing input built by concatenation. <sub>Identity review of #341; Identity review of #420; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Encode strings into a caller-provided span (stackalloc when small and bounded, otherwise rented) with `Encoding.GetBytes(string, Span<byte>)`, and declare fixed protocol or crypto labels (HKDF info, purposes) as `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` `"label"u8` properties instead of `const string` values encoded on every call.** The array-returning overload allocates on every call, and u8 literals need no encoding or allocation at runtime. *Check:* Flag `Encoding.*.GetBytes(str)` whose `byte[]` result is used only briefly, and `const string` labels passed through `GetBytes` before HKDF, HMAC or hashing. <sub>Identity review of #420; Identity review of #341</sub>
